root_cause.text: `nci_close_device()` in the NFC NCI core flushed `rx_wq` while holding `ndev->req_lock`, but `nci_rx_work()` can also indirectly acquire the same mutex via `nci_data_exchange_complete()` → socket teardown → `nci_deactivate_target()` → `nci_request()`, creating a circular lock dependency/deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq);` from inside `nci_close_device()`’s `req_lock`-protected section to after `mutex_unlock(&ndev->req_lock)`, and the commit message explicitly states that `nci_rx_work` can end up taking `req_lock` too through the call chain `nci_rx_work -> nci_rx_data_packet -> nci_data_exchange_complete -> __sk_destruct -> rawsock_destruct -> nfc_deactivate_target -> nci_deactivate_target -> nci_request -> mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust nci_close_device() teardown to avoid flushing the RX workqueue under the lock while still flushing TX work.
intent_record.what: In nci_close_device(), the call to flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq) was removed, the comment was changed from "Flush RX and TX wq" to "Flush TX wq, RX wq flush can't be under the lock", and flush_workqueue(ndev->tx_wq) remains.
intent_record.how: At runtime, device close no longer flushes the RX workqueue in this code path, avoiding flushing RX work while holding the lock; only the TX workqueue is flushed here, which changes the teardown ordering and prevents a lock-related issue.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify nci_close_device shutdown comments to reflect that RX work may still run after close and that the command workqueue flush also covers TX work.
intent_record.what: In nci_close_device(), the comment above ndev->ops->close() was changed to state that rx work may still be running but will observe NCI_UP being cleared, and the comment above flush_workqueue(ndev->cmd_wq) was changed from "Flush cmd wq" to "Flush cmd and tx wq".
intent_record.how: The runtime behavior is unchanged by the code itself, but the updated comments document that close() no longer assumes all work has stopped before it returns, and that flushing the command workqueue also covers transmit-related work. This clarifies the shutdown sequence and the synchronization expectations during device close.

intent_record.intent_summary: Flush rx work during device close to prevent races with teardown and req_lock usage.
intent_record.what: In nci_close_device(), after unlocking ndev->req_lock, the code now calls flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq) and adds a comment noting that rx_work may take req_lock via nci_deactivate_target.
intent_record.how: This ensures any pending receive work on ndev->rx_wq completes before the device close path returns, preventing work items from racing with teardown and potentially re-acquiring req_lock after it has been released in the close sequence.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure device close teardown safely flushes RX/TX work to prevent races with lock usage.

relevance_review.reason: The changes target nci_close_device() teardown and specifically the RX work flush/req_lock interaction described in the root cause. Adjusting when RX work is flushed during close is directly related to preventing the circular lock dependency/deadlock.

The change touches nci_close_device shutdown behavior and explicitly discusses RX work running after close, which is directly related to the deadlock root cause involving rx_wq flushing during close and concurrent RX work paths.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct problematic operation: flushing the RX workqueue while still inside the close path can run nci_rx_work() under req_lock, and that work may re-enter lock acquisition through nci_data_exchange_complete() -> socket teardown -> nci_deactivate_target() -> nci_request(), creating the deadlock.
The deadlock depends on req_lock being held across the RX workqueue flush; this unlock occurs after the flush in the pre-fix flow, so it is part of the vulnerable lock-holding region.

vuln_statements.explanation: This flushes the RX workqueue while ndev->req_lock is still held in nci_close_device(), which can deadlock if nci_rx_work() re-enters the same mutex through nci_data_exchange_complete() -> socket teardown -> nci_deactivate_target() -> nci_request().
In the pre-fix flow, this unlock happens only after the RX workqueue flush, meaning req_lock is held across the deadlock-prone flush and is part of the vulnerable lock-holding region.
